check_details: Reviewer ran mocha on the four changed test files at the reviewed head: 27 passing, 0 failing.

Reviewer ran a scratch script under the work directory comparing the constructor's stack handling for the old and new test input: the old input gets a freshly captured stack, the new one reuses the original's.

findings.title: Restore the no-stack case in the GraphQLError stack test
findings.trigger: The test 'creates new stack if original error has no stack' now passes `new Error('original')`, which always carries a stack, instead of the stack-less `{ message: 'original' }` it used at the merge-base.
findings.impact: The constructor's `originalError && originalError.stack` fallthrough is no longer exercised with an original error lacking a stack, so a change such as `if (originalError)` passes the suite; the merge-base test would have failed it. The test now duplicates 'uses the stack of an original error'.
findings.change: In that test, keep the Flow-valid Error but clear its stack, for example `const original: any = new Error('original'); original.stack = undefined;`, so the no-stack path is exercised again.

observations.fact: The implementation signature still types `nodes` without `null`, although the body treats `null` like `undefined` through a truthiness check.
The `| null` addition implements the point the author raised in their own review thread on `src/error/GraphQLError.js:25`.
observations.evidence: `src/error/GraphQLError.js:25`; the thread text came from the caller's PR text, with no forge access to re-read it.
